questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Namibia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Namibia article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Namibia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Namibia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Namibia article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by the countries of Angola and Zambia to the north, Botswana to the east, and South Africa to the south.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Namibia?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Namibia article.

questions.proof: German is still widely spoken in the country, although English is the official language.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It does not border the country of _____, but it is very close to it.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “country”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Namibia article.

questions.proof: It does not border the country of Zimbabwe, but it is very close to it.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It gained independence from South Africa in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Namibia article.

questions.proof: It gained independence from South Africa in 1990.
